en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic to the forests of the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government, called Congress, is responsible for creating and passing national laws.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato are renowned for weaving t'nalak, a cloth made from abaca fibers.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where characters represent syllables, used by early Filipinos before Spanish colonization.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, a pioneering Filipino pediatrician, invented an improvised bamboo incubator for rural areas without electricity.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan to honor Andres Bonifacio and the Katipuneros.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
